recommendation_summary: Act now: keep the shared folder for drafts and add a Released folder. Only the three reviewers can add files there; authors can read but not edit. Reviewers save each approved document there as a PDF. The platform's audit log records who added each file and when, and a 7-year retention policy on the folder stops files being deleted or replaced. No optional additions are offered. Unmet needs: the setup assumes no reviewer approves a document they wrote, and that the platform supports retention policies and audit logs; the reply asks which platform it is and whether reviewers also write documents. It does not make sure the audit log itself is kept for 7 years.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The customer contract requires each released document to keep its exact approved version, approver identity, and approval time for 7 years, bars authors from approving their own documents, and bars later edits from changing the approved version. You asked to ship this week and keep the folder.
labels.Deleted: The typed-initials APPROVED column and naming convention as controls, and any new document or workflow system.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can edit everything in the one shared folder, so no approved version stays fixed.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me. I have not seen the folder's platform, permissions, or retention settings.

note: The choice is an enforceable setup of existing tools, but the approver and time record lives in an audit log that is never kept for the 7-year period, and the non-author rule holds only if reviewers don't write documents.
